signal.title: CEFAS26-109 RFQ for Sediment Coring Survey Services aboard RV Cefas Endeavour
signal.description: Cefas requires the provision of specialist marine geotechnical services to support two vibracoring surveys within the Irish Sea Firth of Clyde or North Sea. The Supplier is required to achieve sediment cores each with a target penetration of up to 3 m from pre-planned stations for the delivery of our environmental sampling programme. The Supplier is required to provide a 3 metre vibrocorer, complete with spares, coring consumables (coring liners etc) core splitting and core cutting equipment, and suitable individuals to undertake operations of the vibrocorer on a 24 hrs period (2 x 12 hrs shifts back-to-back) alongside deck crew. The Supplier’s personnel will be accommodated onboard the RV Cefas Endeavour for the duration of the survey. Cefas will provide suitable onboard cabin accommodation, bedding and welfare facilities, together with meals and refreshments as part of the vessel’s normal catering provision. The RV Cefas Endeavour has en-suite accommodation for scientific and technical personnel. The Supplier should therefore not include separate accommodation or subsistence costs for periods spent onboard the vessel. Any specific dietary requirements should be notified to Cefas in advance of mobilisation. The Supplier will remain responsible for all travel and associated costs required to mobilise and demobilise its personnel and equipment to/from the agreed port, unless otherwise stated. This should be reflected in the quote provided. The survey is scheduled for approximately ten to twelve days between the 1st to the 16th of November with the flexibility of +/- 5 days each side, with the availability to mobilise and demobilise equipment either in Lowestoft or a Port on the Southwest coast. The port will be confirmed by Cefas as soon as possible. Suppliers must be prepared to mobilise and demobilise from either location. Suppliers must provide evidence of valid and appropriate offshore survival training and medical certification, including BOSIET or STCW95 and a UK Offshore Operators Association-approved medical, or suitable equivalents. Original hard copies of all required certification and documentation will be required for inspection upon request at the time of vessel mobilisation. Please note general arrangement drawings of the RV Cefas Endeavour can be supplied upon Contract award for operational logistics if required. Requirement: The Supplier will liaise with Cefas before mobilisation to confirm the operational requirements, vessel interfaces, equipment layout, power supply, lifting arrangements, programme and health and safety requirements. A mobilisation plan shall be prepared and agreed by both parties in advance of installation. The Supplier will provide a fully maintained and function-tested 3 m high-powered vibrocorer spread, including its control system, constant-tension winch, core barrels, workshop container, essential spares and associated ancillary equipment. The proposed system shall be suitable for operations in water depths of approximately 150 m. The vibrocorer spread shall be delivered to the nominated mobilisation port and installed aboard the RV Cefas Endeavour. Following installation, the Supplier will complete appropriate equipment inspections, function tests and deployment checks, including a wet test where practicable. The Supplier will provide suitably trained and experienced equipment technicians to install, operate, maintain and demobilise the vibrocoring equipment. The base provision shall comprise of four technicians for operations of up to 24 hours per day (two technicians per 12-hour shift). The two technicians will be supported by RV Cefas Endeavour crew for the safe deployment and recovery of equipment. At each survey location, the vessel shall establish a safe and stable working position before the vibrocorer is deployed to the seabed using the vessel’s suitable crane or A-frame and lifting winch. Cefas shall provide the station position and water-depth information for each deployment. Once seabed conditions and the survey position have been confirmed, the vibrocorer shall be operated until either: • the full available barrel penetration is achieved; • refusal is encountered due to the ground conditions; or • the deployment is stopped for operational or safety reasons. Following each attempt, the vibrocorer shall be recovered to deck and the retained sediment core removed from the barrel, visually inspected, split and transferred to Cefas personnel. The Supplier will undertake the acquisition of the sediment cores and check the samples and associated acquisition information before handing them to Cefas. Unless otherwise agreed, laboratory testing, detailed data processing, interpretation, and reporting are outside the Suppliers scope. The Supplier will maintain the vibrocorer spread throughout the offshore programme and provide suitable spare parts for key components to minimise operational downtime. Any equipment defects shall be reported promptly to the Cefas Survey Lead, together with proposed corrective action and any expected effect on the programme. The proposed provision includes full spares coverage for key components. On completion of the offshore work, the Supplier will safely isolate, dismantle and remove its equipment from the vessel at the nominated demobilisation port. The work area shall be left in a safe and satisfactory condition. The Supplier will carry out the Services in accordance with its approved health and safety and quality-management procedures, Cefas vessel requirements and all applicable legislation, including the Lifting Operations and Lifting Equipment Regulations 1998 (LOLER), where applicable. All offshore activities shall be appropriately risk assessed, and suitable method statements, lifting plans and operational procedures shall be agreed before mobilisation. All lifting equipment and accessories shall be suitable for the intended operation, appropriately certified and subject to the required examination and inspection regime. Download the Bidder Pack at https://defra-family.force.com/s/Welcome and search for CEFAS26-109 under opportunities.

signal.title: Transport Phenomena (TP)
signal.description: The Transport Phenomena (TP) program supports fundamental research to understand, model, and control the transport of mass, momentum, energy, and species across multiple scales. Innovative TP research supports advances in artificial intelligence; manufacturing; biotechnology; microelectronics; energy generation, extraction, and utilization; nuclear energy; quantum science and engineering; and other national priorities. TP projects involve experiments, theory, and/or computational modeling. They aim to improve understanding and to create novel analytical techniques. While projects focus on fundamental principles, they also have a clear vision of how research outcomes will benefit applications in engineering. TP supports research on the dynamics of single- and multiphase systems. Special interests include flow separation, transition to turbulence, drag reduction, cavitation, instabilities, and reactive flows. The program encourages research on the connection between dynamics at the microscale and material and flow properties at the macroscale. Fluids of interest include liquids, gases, suspensions, emulsions, granular materials, active fluids, biological fluids, colloids, aerosols, bubbles and drops, and fluids with surfactants. TP supports research on physicochemical phenomena at the interfaces between fluids and between fluids and solids. These phenomena include adsorption and desorption of nanoparticles and surfactants; bulk and interfacial rheology; wetting and capillarity phenomena; electrokinetics; flow in porous media; and directed and self-assembly of particles. TP supports research on thermodynamics and thermal transport involving conduction, diffusion, convection, phase transition, and radiation. Research may be across scales, in complex structures and at interfaces, in microelectronic devices, and in biological systems. Projects involving phonon transport and quantum thermal phenomena are welcome. TP encourages proposals focused on combustion of gas, liquid and solid fuels. Combustion topics of interest include chemical kinetic modeling, turbulence-chemistry interactions, detonations, plasma assisted reacting flows, sustainable fuels, mechanisms for pollutant control, and in-situ diagnostic methods. The program also supports research on wildland fire behavior that aims to prevent wildfire spread, inhibit its growth, and/or predict and mitigate fires at the wildland-urban interface. Partnerships: To speed discovery and innovation, NSF partners with federal agencies, industry, international groups, and others. Current opportunities are at NSF ENG Partnerships.

signal.title: Recruitment Services: Circular Economy Intern Placements
signal.description: The Zero Waste Scotland Circular Economy Intern Programme was launched in 2020 to support businesses to identify, design and deliver circular economy practices by providing access to additional, resources for circular economy projects. The programme was developed in recognition of a key barrier faced by many organisations: limited internal capacity to explore and implement circular economy approaches alongside day-to-day operations. There remains a strong and ongoing role for an intern programme of this nature and Zero Waste Scotland would like to contract with a suitable organisation to recruit, manage and report on a series of internships to be placed within different enterprises in Scotland to support transition to circular business models Lot 1: . Zero Waste Scotland (the ‘Client’) requires the provision of technical support from a suitably skilled and experienced third-party organisation to recruit and manage a series of internships to be placed within different enterprises in Scotland to support transition to circular business models The Contractor shall work closely with the Client to provide recruitment services that facilitate the identification, recruitment and placement of suitably qualified candidates into internship placements within Client-approved host enterprises. Placements shall be offered on a call-off basis for a duration of up to 12 months, for a maximum of thirty-five (35) hours per week. The exact duration of each placement will vary depending on the agreed scope, objectives and requirements of the individual placement, as approved by the Client. The services to be provided by the Contractor may include, either individually or in combination, and with input from the Client and the host enterprise as appropriate, the following: -Development of a suitable job description for each placement, aligned with the agreed scope and objectives. -Advertisement of the internship opportunity through appropriate and agreed recruitment/ media channels. -Shortlisting of suitable candidates against agreed selection criteria. -Coordination and conduct of interviews with suitable shortlisted candidates, in collaboration with the Client and host enterprise. -Contract management of the intern for the duration of the placement. -Provision of all payroll requirements required for the placement, including statutory obligations. -Exit management of the intern at the end of the placement, including end of contract processes.

signal.title: Erfahrungsaustausch zu Vergrämungsmaßnahmen (Los 1) und Planung von koordinierten Vergrämungsabschüssen (Los 2) für das Interreg-Projekt "Fischartenschutz und Kormoranmanagement am Bodensee"
signal.description: Kurzzusammenfassung des Interreg-Projekts "Fischartenschutz und Kormoranmanagement am Bodensee": Durch internationale, mit allen Bodensee-Anrainern abgestimmte, Maßnahmen soll der Schutz gefährdeter Fischarten in der Bodenseeregion verstärkt vorangetrieben werden. Das Wissen über gefährdete Fischarten in der Region wird im Rahmen des Projekts zusammengetragen und darauf aufbauend Maßnahmen zur Verbesserung ihres Schutzes erarbeitet. Die Maßnahmen beinhalten neben ökologischen Aufwertungen der Fischhabitate auch technische Schutzmaßnahmen gegen Kormoranfraß. Daten werden in einer Datenbank erfasst und wasserbautechnische "Musterlösungen" erarbeitet. Zur Reduktion des Fraßdrucks durch Kormorane auf gefährdete Fischarten werden Grundlagen erarbeitet, welche auf eine internationale Strategie zum Kormoranmanagement abzielen. Diese beinhalten auch den Einsatz modernster Drohnentechnologie zum Brutmanagement der Kormorane. Dabei soll die Eignung und Bewilligungsfähigkeit von regionalen Maßnahmen zum Kormoranmanagement und ihrer grenzüberschreitenden Wirkung geklärt werden. Lot LOT-0001: Erfahrungsaustausch zu Vergrämungsmaßnahmen. Recherchearbeit mit anschließender Evaluation von Erfahrungen mit örtlichen und zeitlich befristeten Vergrämungsmaßnahmen gegen Kormorane in der Bodenseeregion sowie in anderen Regionen Europas. Anschließend sollen Konzepte für besonders gefährdete Teilpopulationen gefährdeter Fischarten in der Bodenseeregion entwickelt werden. Dazu sind - aufbauend auf den Ergebnissen von Arbeitspaket 3a1, welches die Zeiten und Orte mit erhöhter Kormoranprädation im Bodenseegebiet ermittelt - mögliche Vergrämungsmaßnahmen für Kormorane an Fließgewässern zu recherchieren und im Hinblick auf ihre Eignung in Bezug auf die jeweiligen örtlichen Verhältnisse zu bewerten und zu konzeptionieren. Dabei sollen bestimmte Fischpopulationen der Fokus-Fischarten (z.B. Äschenpopulationen von europäischer bzw. gesamtschweizerischer Bedeutung) prioritär behandelt werden. Zusätzlich sollen in bestimmten Teilen des Sees und des Einzugsgebiets (z.B. Konstanzer Trichter, Seerhein), an welchen die Kormoranprädation erhebliche Schäden an geschützten / gefährdeten Fischarten verursacht, Maßnahmen-Konzepte ausgearbeitet werden, wie der Fischartenschutz durch gezielte Vergrämungsmaßnahmen verbessert werden kann. Lot LOT-0002: Planung von koordinierten Vergrämungsabschüssen. Vergrämungsabschüsse von Kormoranen im Winterhalbjahr sind in den Ländern und Kantonen rund um den See unter Einhaltung der jeweiligen rechtlichen Bestimmungen prinzipiell zulässig. Diese erfolgen nach bisherigem Kenntnisstand anlassbezogen und unkoordiniert. Der daraus resultierende Effekt zur Reduktion von Kormoranfraß ist deshalb fraglich, insbesondere auf die Fokusfischarten des Interreg-Projektes. Demgegenüber könnten von unkoordinierten Vergrämungsabschüssen Störungen von Schutzgütern, wie z.B. rastenden Wasservogelarten, ausgehen. Durch eine bodensee-weit koordinierte Vergrämung von Kormoranen soll diese Situation verbessert werden. Dazu bedarf es einer Recherche zum Ist-Zustand mit anschließender Konzeptionierung einer Koordination von Vergrämungsabschüssen in der Bodenseeregion. Ziel ist die Optimierung der Reduktion von Kormoranprädation auf gefährdete Fischarten, insbesondere der Fokusfischarten, vom Herbst bis ins Frühjahr. Diese soll in den verschiedenen Anrainerländern am Bodensee durch Vernetzung der Akteure und Koordination aller Vergrämungsabschüsse erreicht werden.

translation.description: Brief summary of the Interreg project "Fish species conservation and cormorant management on Lake Constance": Through international measures coordinated with all riparian states of Lake Constance, the protection of endangered fish species in the Lake Constance region is to be decisively advanced. Knowledge about endangered fish species in the region is compiled within the framework of the project and, building on this, measures to improve their protection are developed. In addition to ecological enhancements of fish habitats, the measures also include technical protection measures against cormorant predation. Data are recorded in a database and hydraulic engineering "model solutions" are developed. To reduce the predation pressure by cormorants on endangered fish species, fundamentals are developed which aim at an international strategy for cormorant management. These also include the use of state-of-the-art drone technology for breeding management of cormorants. In this context, the suitability and approvability of regional measures for cormorant management and their cross-border impact are to be clarified. Lot LOT-0001: Exchange of experience on deterrent measures. Research work with subsequent evaluation of experiences with local and temporally restricted deterrent measures against cormorants in the Lake Constance region as well as in other regions of Europe. Subsequently, concepts for particularly endangered sub-populations of endangered fish species in the Lake Constance region are to be developed. For this purpose - building on the results of work package 3a1, which determines the times and locations with increased cormorant predation in the Lake Constance area - possible deterrent measures for cormorants on flowing waters are to be researched and evaluated and conceptualised with regard to their suitability in relation to the respective local conditions. Certain fish populations of the focus fish species (e.g. grayling populations of European or pan-Swiss significance) are to be given priority treatment. In addition, in certain parts of the lake and the catchment area (e.g. Constance funnel, Seerhein), where cormorant predation causes considerable damage to protected / endangered fish species, measure concepts are to be drawn up on how fish species conservation can be improved by targeted deterrent measures. Lot LOT-0002: Planning of coordinated deterrent culls. Deterrent culls of cormorants in the winter half-year are principally permissible in the federal states and cantons around the lake in compliance with the respective legal provisions. According to previous knowledge, these take place on an ad-hoc and uncoordinated basis. The resulting effect for the reduction of cormorant feeding is therefore questionable, in particular on the focus fish species of the Interreg project. In contrast, uncoordinated deterrent culls could cause disturbances to objects of protection, such as resting waterbird species. This situation is to be improved by a Lake Constance-wide coordinated deterrence of cormorants. This requires research into the current status followed by the conceptualisation of a coordination of deterrent culls in the Lake Constance region. The aim is to optimise the reduction of cormorant predation on endangered fish species, in particular the focus fish species, from autumn to spring. This is to be achieved in the various riparian countries on Lake Constance by networking the actors and coordinating all deterrent culls.
translation.title: Exchange of experience on deterrent measures (lot 1) and planning of coordinated deterrent culls (lot 2) for the Interreg project "Fish species conservation and cormorant management on Lake Constance"

signal.title: Internal Audit Services - Adra and Grwp Cynefin
signal.description: Adra Tai Cyfyngedig (“Adra”) and Grŵp Cynefin are two separate housing associations based in north Wales. We are currently exploring our options for the future provision of our internal audit services, including whether a joint procurement approach would be beneficial. To help us determine our next steps, we welcome early engagement from suitably experienced internal audit providers to help us understand market interest, capacity and views on the proposed approach. If a joint procurement is pursued, it is anticipated that each housing association would enter into separate contracts with the successful provider. Adra: Adra is North Wales’ largest housing association, providing more than 7,500 quality, affordable homes and services to people in housing need across the region, while supporting the culture and heritage of the communities it serves; it is a charitable registered society regulated by the Welsh Government. Adra is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced provider to deliver an independent, objective and collaborative internal audit service focused on its core governance, service delivery, financial risks and internal controls, supporting both its landlord activities and wider priorities such as decarbonisation, development and growth. The anticipated requirement is approximately 40 days per year and will include recurring compliance and data integrity audits, selected strategic audits in key risk areas, cyclical follow-up of recommendations, development of the Internal Audit Strategy and Annual Audit Plan, timely reporting on individual audits, an annual assurance opinion, limited desktop compliance and data integrity testing within landlord health and safety areas, and attendance at relevant Board or Committee meetings where required. Whilst much of the contract specification could be delivered remotely, there will at times be an expectation for relevant representatives to occasionally attend the office or locations throughout North Wales. This may include attendance at Board and/or Committee Meetings, to present findings and reports. Grŵp Cynefin: Grŵp Cynefin is a charitable housing association and registered society regulated by the Welsh Government, owning approximately 5,000 homes across six counties in north Wales and north Powys. Grŵp Cynefin is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced provider to deliver an independent, objective and risk-based internal audit service covering governance, risk management, financial and operational controls, regulatory compliance and service delivery. The anticipated requirement is approximately 68 days per year and will include an internal audit strategy and risk-based annual audit plan, delivery of individual audits with timely reporting, follow-up of recommendations, an annual assurance opinion, and reporting to and attendance at the Audit and Risk Committee and Board where required. Much of the service can be delivered remotely, with attendance at its offices or other locations in north Wales expected from time to time, including to present findings. We would be pleased to hear from potential bidders who may be interested in this opportunity. Your response will help Adra and Grŵp Cynefin understand the level of market interest and determine whether it is beneficial to proceed with a joint procurement exercise. Please respond by 21 September 2026. We would also welcome an informal discussion with if you would like to explore the requirements, ask questions or provide any feedback before responding. To arrange any discussions and to provide any feedback, please contact caffael@adra.co.uk If you do not intend to bid, we would still appreciate hearing your reasons, as this will provide valuable insight into the market and help inform our approach. Next steps: Following receipt of the Expressions of Interest, Adra and Grŵp Cynefin will review the feedback and decide whether to proceed collaboratively or undertake separate procurement exercises. We anticipate that the tender opportunity will be published by the end of September 2026, for the contracts to be effective from the 1st of April 2027. Further details on the proposed procurement timetable and process will be shared once this decision has been made. Please note that this is for market engagement only, with no commitment to proceed, no costs reimbursed and no bearing on whether a supplier can tender later. Lot 1: . None

signal.description: The contracting authority needs to enter into a framework agreement with a tenderer for the procurement of communication and marketing services. Please note that job advertisements and film production will not be included in this framework agreement. See chapter 4 for further details on the procurement ́s purpose and requirements. The contracting authority is uncertain about the extent of the procurement, but based on average calculations based on statistics information for 2023-2025, an annual contract value of approx. NOK 1,200,000 is estimated excluding VAT. The total estimated contract value, including options, is approx. NOK 4,800,000 excluding VAT. Emphasis is put on the fact that the estimated contract value is only of an informative character and does not represent any obligations for the contracting authority or rights for the tenderer. The contracting authority draws attention to the fact that the actual contract value can vary, partly as a result of a decision that municipal sub-plans and other types of plans are likely to be prepared internally in the municipality, as well as changed financial framework terms, organisational changes and municipal activity. Tenderers cannot demand compensation if the expected procurement is lower than expected. Based on the estimated value of the contract, the contracting authority has stated the maximum contract value, c.f. the Court of Justice's case C-23/20. The maximum contract value is + 15% above the estimated value, calculated to NOK 5,520,000 excluding VAT.

Die ehemalige Bebauung sowie die Oberflächenbeläge wurden bereits zurückgebaut. Das Schulgrundstück selbst liegt an der südlich verlaufenden Schönburger Straße sowie an der östlich verlaufenden, im Zuge des B- Plan- Verfahrens neu geplanten und errichteten Dr. - Wilhelm- Kniest- Straße zwischen der Schönburger Straße und der Grochlitzer Straße an. Zum Campus gehört noch das Grundstück mit der Flurstücksnummer 692. Das Straßenquartier zwischen Schönburger- , Rosa-Luxemburg und Grochlitzer Straße ist gekennzeichnet durch eine weitgehend homogen wirkende Bebauung durch meist dreigeschossige Wohngebäude. Das Grundstück ist weitgehend eben und umfasst eine Fläche von 25.196m2. Die baulichen Anlagen des neuen Schulcampus werden auf drei Gebäudebereiche verteilt . In der Angebotsaufforderung sind die Gebäudeteile des Bauvorhabens wie folgt bezeichnet: Teilobjekt A Schulgebäude Das Gebäude, d as die Schulräume der Förderschule, d er Sekundarschule und Teile des BVJ beherbergt, bildet als größte Baumasse das Zentrum der Anlage und ist selbst in drei „ Gebäudekuben“ gegliedert, höhenmäßig gestaffelt zwischen zwei und vier Obergeschossen. translation.description: The Burgenlandkreis acting as the client intends to construct a new school campus on the "Stadtquartier Schönburger Straße" site, consisting of a school building and a 3-field sports hall. The Centre for the Vocational Preparation Year (BVJ), which is also planned on the site, is not the subject of this tender. The construction site for the planned new campus building is located east of the Naumburg centre within the scope of a legally binding development plan (B-Plan No. 62 "Stadtquartier Schönburger Straße"). The former buildings and surface pavings have already been dismantled. The school property itself is situated on Schönburger Straße running to the south and on Dr-Wilhelm-Kniest-Straße, newly planned and constructed in the course of the development plan procedure, between Schönburger Straße and Grochlitzer Straße to the east. The campus also includes the plot with the plot number 692. The street quarter between Schönburger Straße, Rosa-Luxemburg-Straße and Grochlitzer Straße is characterised by largely homogeneous buildings consisting mostly of three-storey residential buildings. The plot is largely flat and covers an area of 25.196 m2. The structures of the new school campus are distributed across three building areas. In the invitation to tender, the building parts of the construction project are designated as follows: Sub-project A School building The building, which houses the school rooms of the special needs school, the secondary school and parts of the BVJ, forms the centre of the facility as the largest building mass and is itself structured into three "building cubes", staggered in height between two and four upper floors. The three building section areas are each structured around an inner courtyard core. The buildings are constructed using solid construction methods with load-bearing walls and columns made of reinforced concrete as well as reinforced concrete ceilings with a flat roof. The foundation is laid on reinforced concrete floor slabs. The middle building section (A 1) has a basement, while the northern and southern building sections (A2 and A3) do not have basements. Sub-project B Sports hall The three-field sports hall is arranged to the north adjacent to the school building. A two-storey functional wing adjoins the southern longitudinal side of the large hall room with DIN dimensions (4 5 x 2 7 m). The building foundation for the social wing is constructed as a slab foundation with reinforced concrete floor slabs, while the hall is founded on individual foundations and strip foundations beneath the external walls. The load-bearing walls, columns and floor slabs in the social wing are constructed in reinforced concrete. The hall roof is designed with glued laminated timber girders and a load-bearing shell made of trapezoidal profiled steel sheeting. signal.title: Rahmenvereinbarung mit einem Handelspartner für die Beschaffung von Adobe Creative Cloud Lizenzen
signal.description: Gegenstand und Ziel ist eine Rahmenvereinbarung mit einem Handelspartner über den Bezug von Lizenzen für Softwareprodukte und sonstige damit zusammenhängende Leistungen der Firma Adobe nach dem Lizenzierungsprogramm Value Incentive Plan Marketplace (VIP MP). Darüber hinaus sind Leistungen zu erbringen, die im Zusammenhang mit dem Bezug der Lizenzen stehen, insbesondere Lizenzberatung (inkl. technischer Bewertung) und Reporting-Leistungen. Die Lecos GmbH, die Stadt Leipzig und verschiedene Eigenbetriebe der Stadt Leipzig verfügen über Adobe VIP Marketplace Verträge. Über die Lecos GmbH laufen dabei die Beschaffung von Softwareprodukten sowie sämtliche Kommunikation und Abwicklung zu diesen Verträgen. Die Lecos GmbH ist berechtigt, diese Verträge zu schließen. Die Verträge sind teilweise über ein Linked Membership verbunden. Es ist angedacht, für einige Verträge ein 3-year-commit abzuschließen. Es sollen vorhandene Lizenzen für Softwareprodukte verlängert bzw. über neue Verträge weitergeführt und Neulizenzen hinzugekauft werden. Zusätzliche Verträge können während der Laufzeit der Rahmenvereinbarung hinzukommen. Die vorhandenen Verträge wurden als "Commercial" eröffnet. Die Verlängerung der Lizenzen ist gegebenenfalls über "Government"-Verträge geplant. Zudem gibt es Bestrebungen, Verträge durch "Non-Profit"-Verträge zu ersetzen. Der Handelspartner muss diese Segmente ebenfalls bedienen können. Es wird ausschließlich der Bezug über Adobe VIP Marketplace ausgeschrieben. Der Bezug über einen Adobe Enterprise Terms License Agreement (ETLA) wurde im Vorfeld geprüft und ausgeschlossen. signal.title: Provision of Off-Site Storage for NatureScot Records
signal.description: NatureScot is preparing to undertake a procurement exercise for the Provision of Off-Site Storage. As part of the development process for the procurement approach, NatureScot is seeking views and information from the marketplace in connection with the areas set out in this Prior Information Notice (PIN). NatureScot have included a questionnaire (which can be found here - https://www.cognitoforms.com/ScotlandExcel1/OnBehalfOfNatureScotScottishNaturalHeritageOffsiteStorageForNatureScotRecords) Lot 1: . NatureScot is preparing to undertake a procurement exercise for the Provision of Off-Site Storage. The future contract is expected to run for an initial five-year period, with the option to extend for up to two further years, providing a potential total duration of seven years. NatureScot currently stores approximately 5,743 cubic feet of records offsite, consisting of a wide range of formats including paper files, maps, photographs, slides, audiovisual materials, and digital media. These records require secure, environmentally controlled storage, robust inventory management and reliable retrieval and transport arrangements. In addition, the forthcoming requirement is expected to include scan on demand services, secure destruction, and the supply of associated materials such as boxes, barcodes and destruction sacks. The supplier will also need to ensure and maintain full system compatibility with NatureScot’s Electronic Records and Document Management System (eRDMS). Integration will be achieved through API-driven transmission of CSV metadata files from the eRDMS to the Contract’s inventory system. NatureScot requires that, in the event the incumbent supplier does not bid or is not awarded the contract, the successful supplier will be responsible for managing the full transfer of existing records from the incumbent’s facility to their own. This will include all planning, coordination, uplift, transport, and reconciliation of inventory data. Market consultation is an important part of the procurement process and gives us an opportunity to consider your specialist opinion and expertise. This engagement does not constitute the launch of a procurement process; however, responses will help shape the forthcoming Invitation to Tender.. NatureScot have included a questionnaire (which can be found here - https://www.cognitoforms.com/ScotlandExcel1/OnBehalfOfNatureScotScottishNaturalHeritageOffsiteStorageForNatureScotRecords) for interested suppliers and may invite further dialogue to explore delivery models and gather feedback.

signal.title: Helensburgh, Cardross, Dumbarton Cyclepath Active Travel Route - Phase 3: Developed & Technical Design
signal.description: This tender is for Phase 3 of the Helensburgh, Cardross and Dumbarton Cyclepath; linking the Helensburgh Waterfront segregated cycleway (OS Grid NS 29598 82259) to the existing section of the cyclepath adjacent to the A814 at the Red Burn (OS Grid NS 31655 81112), near the north-east corner of Morrisons Supermarket site, and will build upon the concept design developed for the majority of the route (Civic Engineers, 2025). Argyll & Bute Council wish to appoint an appropriately qualified and experienced design team to develop Phase 3 of the Helensburgh, Cardross and Dumbarton Cyclepath project from the current concept design through Developed (RIBA Stage 3) and Technical (RIBA Stage 4) Design, and to be Principal Designer during construction (RIBA Stage 5). The project will require the successful tenderer to complete a range of survey, design and in-depth engagement work, including in-depth community, stakeholder and landowner engagement, topographic and utilities surveys, equality impact assessment (EqIA) and Preliminary Environmental Assessment (PEA) to ensure route(s) identified have strong community, neighbour and landowner support and that the design drawings for the route(s) are robust, deliverable and of a high quality. These will all be subject to engagement with the community, businesses, landowners, neighbouring landowners, Argyll and Bute Council, Strathclyde Partnership for Transport (SPT) and Transport Scotland. signal.title: Postdoctoral Research Fellowships in Biology
signal.description: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Biological Research has the potential to pave the way for breakthroughs in biotechnology and bio-system design that will create innovations, new industries, and jobs. To capitalize on this promise, the Directorate for Biological Sciences (BIO) will make awards for Postdoctoral Research Fellowships in Biology (PRFB) to recent doctoral degree recipients, for proposals with a research and training focus at the Intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Biological Sciences to Strengthen and Safeguard Biotechnology Innovations. Applying AI to highly complex biological systems will reveal unknown mechanisms in the natural world that hold promise for technological developments. Candidates with AI and/or biology experience will develop deep expertise in both by proposing additional training in both areas. These combinations of current expertise and new cross-training will produce scientists who work seamlessly at the intersection of AI and biology. The fellows are expected to become field leaders who use AI capabilities to extrapolate from biological data to technological advances. Proposers are encouraged to consider how to leverage the nation’s diversity of existing biological data, and biological infrastructure, such as Biofoundries, Programmable Cloud Labs, Manufacturing USA Institutes, and NEON, to accelerate discovery, innovation and the biotechnology that improves human lives, promotes the U.S. economy, and benefits the nation.

signal.title: Fire Alarm Design, Installation, and Associated Project Management Services DPS
signal.description: The Scottish Government is looking to establish a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for Fire Alarm Design, Installation & Associated Project Management Services. The DPS will be split into 2 Lots: Lot 1: Fire Alarm Design & Installation Lot 2: Associated Project Management Services Please Note: The value of call off- contracts will range from Thousands to Millions however no form of volume guarantee has been granted by the authority and therefore no commitment of spend is guarenteed through the DPS. Lot 2: Associated Project Management Services. Lot 2 of the DPS will comprise of suitably qualified and experienced suppliers to provide project management and contract administration services associated with the delivery of fire detection and fire alarm systems in residential buildings affected by cladding related fire risk across Scotland. Services may include: Coordination of surveys, investigations and technical assessments Preparation of specifications and procurement documentation Tender and contract management Coordination of contractors undertaking opening up, enabling and making good works associated with fire alarm installations Coordination and submission of Building Warrants, approvals, or any other statutory permissions or consents required for the works Resident and Factor liaison Coordination of installation works in occupied buildings Programme, cost and compliance monitoring Oversight of commissioning, testing and certification Coordination of handover documentation and project close out Services will support delivery of works in accordance with BS 5839 and relevant Scottish fire safety legislation, standards and guidance. Projects may include temporary or permanent systems, upgrades to existing installations, and works integrated with wider fire safety or cladding remediation programmes. Core Certification & Regulatory Compliance If asked at call-off contract stage and/or DPS example stage suppliers must demonstrate full compliance and provide certificates if applicable with the following: Relevant construction, engineering or building surveying qualification, such as a degree, HNC/HND, or equivalent in a related discipline (e.g. Building Surveying, Quantity Surveying, Civil Engineering, Architecture or similar) Membership of a relevant professional body, such as: RICS IFE CIOB APM ICE CIBSE RIBA/RIAS Personnel responsible for managing and delivering site based works must hold qualifications and training appropriate to their role when asked for within the call off contract, such as SMSTS, SSSTS, IOSH Managing Safely, CSCS/ECS cards or equivalent industry recognised qualifications. Lot 1: Fire Alarm Design and Installation. Lot 1 of DPS will provide for works in accordance with BS 5839-1:2025 and all relevant Scottish fire safety legislation, standards, and guidance, including requirements under the Fire (Scotland) Act 2005, and applicable Scottish Building Standards. Works may include the provision of new or enhanced fire detection and alarm systems comprising categories L1–L5, as identified through the Single Building Assessment (SBA). Requirements may include temporary or permanent fire alarm solutions, modifications to existing systems, associated enabling works, certification, compliance documentation, integration with wider fire safety strategies or cladding remediation activities and maintenance. Suppliers must be able demonstrate full compliance and provide certificates if applicable with the following if asked for at call off stage and/or within the SPD Example Section: Fire Detection and Alarm System (FD&AS) Standards BS 5839-1:2025 Fire detection and fire alarm systems for Buildings BAFE SP203 1 certification (modules: Design, Installation, Commissioning) Certification body must be UKAS accredited Commissioning shall be conducted in accordance BSRIA Application Guides and CIBSE Commissioning Codes Electrical Design & Installation (Mandatory) BS 7671:2018+A2:2022, Requirements for Electrical Installations BS 5839 1 interface requirements for fire alarm systems Electrical installation certification (EIC / Minor Works as applicable) Scottish Regulatory Compliance Compliance with Scottish Building Regulations, including the relevant provisions of the Building Standards Technical Handbooks (Fire and Electrical sections) Demonstrable understanding of: Fire detection and alarm requirements for domestic and non‐domestic buildings, including system selection and coverage in accordance with risk Applicable certification processes, including use of Approved Certifiers of Design and/or Construction where required under Scottish Building Regulations Legal Competency Confirmation that all works are delivered by “competent persons” under fire safety legislation Understanding of duties under: Fire (Scotland) Act Health and Safety: Personnel responsible for managing and delivering site based works must hold qualifications and training appropriate to their role, such as SMSTS, SSSTS, IOSH Managing Safely, CSCS/ECS cards or equivalent industry recognised qualifications.

signal.title: Brut- und Rastvogelerfassung in EU-Vogelschutzgebieten 2027 / 2028
signal.description: Veranlassung Hintergrund Mit Inkrafttreten des novellierten Bundesnaturschutzgesetzes (BNatSchG) am 01.03.2010 ist das Monitoring gemäß EU-Richtlinie 2009/147/EG ("Vogelschutz-Richtlinie") in § 6 BNatSchG eingegliedert worden. Dies umfasst insbesondere die Beobachtung des Erhaltungszustands der europäischen Vogelarten und ihrer Lebensräume. Entsprechend § 7 Abs. 2 Nr. 12 BNatSchG gelten alle in Europa natürlich vorkommenden Vogelarten als "europäische Vogel-arten". Nach Artikel 9 der Fauna-Flora-Habitat (FFH)-Richtlinie (92/43/EWG) beurteilt die EU-Kommission in regelmäßigen Zeitabständen den Beitrag von Natura 2000 zur Verwirklichung der Ziele aus FFH- und Vogelschutz-Richtlinie. Dies erfordert, den Inhalt der Standarddaten-bögen (SDB) in regelmäßigen Abständen anhand verfügbarer Informationen zu jedem Gebiet des Netzes zu aktualisieren (Durchführungsbeschluss der Kommission 2011/484/EU). Dafür sind Informationen zu Beständen, Bestandsentwicklungen und Lebensräumen der gemäß Artikel 4 Absätze (1) und (2) der EU-Richtlinie 2009/147/EG relevanten Arten erforderlich. Das Monitoring in EU-Vogelschutzgebieten (VSG) als Teil des europäischen Natura 2000-Netzes gehört zum Monitoring europäischer Vogelarten und ihrer Lebensräume gemäß § 6 BNatSchG. Als Teilprogramm dient es (gemäß Richtlinien oder Verordnungen 92/43/EWG, 2009/147/EG und 2019/1010) - der Ermittlung von Beständen relevanter Vogelarten mindestens einmalig im sechsjäh-rigen Berichtsturnus für jedes VSG, - der kontinuierlichen Ermittlung der Bestandsentwicklung und gebietsbezogener Erhal-tungszustände maßgeblicher Brutvogelarten, - der kontinuierlichen Ermittlung der Bestandsentwicklung und gebietsbezogener Erhal-tungszustände maßgeblicher Zug- und Gastvogelarten sowie - der standardisierten Erfassung von Habitatinformationen, Beeinträchtigungen und Ge-fährdungen auf der Gesamtfläche der VSG zur umfassenden Bewertung der Erhal-tungszustände relevanter Vogelarten und ihrer Lebensräume. Das standardisierte Monitoring in den VSG in Rheinland-Pfalz begann mit einem Pilotprojekt 2025/2026 in zehn ausgewählten VSG (gemäß Koalitionsvertrag für Rheinland-Pfalz im Zeit-raum 2021-2026). Daher sind die gebietsspezifischen Datengrundlagen und -qualitäten der-zeit vielfach noch unbefriedigend und die Landesdaten erlauben keine Ermittlung statistisch belastbarer Bestandstrends und der Erhaltungszustände für die maßgeblichen Vogelarten in den rheinland-pfälzischen VSG. Dies verhindert insbesondere eine angemessene Prioritäten- und Zielplanung der Naturschutzbehörden für Maßnahmen, um - sofern nicht vorliegend - gute Erhaltungszustände der relevanten Arten zu erreichen. Das hier ausgeschriebene Auf-gabenpaket dient der ergänzenden Erfassung in weiteren VSG mit Hinblick auf den nächsten Vogelschutzbericht im Jahr 2031 (Datenperiode 2023-2028). Die erwarteten Daten dienen der Erfüllung der Berichtspflichten gegenüber der EU nach Artikel 12 der Richtlinie 2009/147/EG und der Verordnung 2019/1010. Perspektivisch (idealerweise ab 2029) sollen alle rheinland-pfälzischen VSG in einem sechsjährigen Berichtsturnus gemäß eines standar-disierten Monitoring-Konzepts erfasst werden (nicht Bestandteil dieser Vergabe). Monitoring in EU-Vogelschutzgebieten 2011 hat die Länderarbeitsgemeinschaft der Vogelschutzwarten (LAG VSW) zusammen mit dem Dachverband Deutscher Avifaunisten e. V. (DDA) und dem Bundesamt für Naturschutz (BfN) Empfehlungen zum Monitoring europäischer Vogelarten und ihrer Lebensräume vorge-legt (LAG VSW et al., 2011). Diese verfolgen das Ziel, einen bundesweit einheitlichen Stan-dard zur Datenerhebung zu formulieren. Dabei lassen die für das Monitoring in VSG genann-ten Grundsätze ausreichend Raum für landesspezifische Anpassungen. Die Ergebnisse des Monitorings bilden die Grundlage für das Gebietsmanagement vor dem Hintergrund der je-weiligen Erhaltungsziele und für die Berichtspflicht nach Art. 12 der Richtlinie 2009/147/EG. Außerdem dienen sie als Referenz für Entscheidungen bei Vor- und Verträglichkeitsprüfun-gen. Zwecks Erhebung von Grundlagendaten in EU-Vogelschutzgebieten zur Verbesserung der Datenqualität für den nächsten Vogelschutzbericht (Berichtsperiode 2023-2028) und zur effi-zienten Planung des zukünftigen VSG-Monitorings, der Umsetzung des "Griechenland-Urteils" (EuGH in einem Vorabentscheidungsersuchen eines griechischen Gerichts nach Art. 267 AEUV, 12.9.2024 - C-66/23) sowie der Umsetzung der "Wiederherstellungsverordnung" (EU-Verordnung 2024/1991), soll dieses Vergabeverfahren Grundlagendaten zu Vorkommen und Verbreitung relevanter Arten gemäß Artikel 4 Absätze (1) und (2) der EU-Richtlinie 2009/147/EG in möglichst allen rheinland-pfälzischen VSG bereitstellen. translation.description:
Reasoning Background With the entry into force of the amended Federal Nature Conservation Act (BNatSchG) on 01.03.2010, monitoring in accordance with EU Directive 2009/147/EC ("Birds Directive") was incorporated into Section 6 of the BNatSchG. This includes, in particular, the observation of the conservation status of European bird species and their habitats. In accordance with Section 7 ( 2) no. 12 of the BNatSchG, all bird species occurring naturally in Europe are considered "European bird species". According to Article 9 of the Habitats Directive (92/43/EEC), the EU Commission assesses at regular intervals the contribution of Natura 2000 to the realisation of the objectives of the Habitats and Birds Directives. This requires the content of the standard data forms (SDF) to be updated at regular intervals based on information available for each site in the network (Commission Implementing Decision 2011/484/EU). For this purpose, information on populations, population trends and habitats of the species relevant according to Article 4 paragraphs (1) and (2) of EU Directive 2009/147/EC is required. Monitoring in EU Special Protection Areas (SPAs) as part of the European Natura 2000 network is part of the monitoring of European bird species and their habitats in accordance with Section 6 of the BNatSchG. As a sub-programme, it serves (in accordance with Directives or Regulations 92/43/EEC, 2009/147/EC and 2019/1010) - the determination of populations of relevant bird species at least once in the six-year reporting cycle for each SPA, - the continuous determination of population trends and site-related conservation statuses of significant breeding bird species, - the continuous determination of population trends and site-related conservation statuses of significant migratory and wintering bird species, and - the standardised recording of habitat information, impairments and threats across the entire area of the SPAs for a comprehensive assessment of the conservation status of relevant bird species and their habitats. Standardised monitoring in the SPAs in Rhineland-Palatinate began with a pilot project 2025/2026 in ten selected SPAs (in accordance with the coalition agreement for Rhineland-Palatinate in the period 2021-2026). Therefore, the site-specific data foundations and qualities are currently often still unsatisfactory, and the state data do not allow for the determination of statistically robust population trends and conservation statuses for the significant bird species in the Rhineland-Palatinate SPAs. This prevents, in particular, appropriate priority and target planning by nature conservation authorities for measures to achieve good conservation status for the relevant species, where this is not already the case. The task package tendered here serves the supplementary recording in further SPAs with a view to the next bird protection report in the year 2031 (data period 2023-2028). The expected data serve to fulfil the reporting obligations to the EU under Article 12 of Directive 2009/147/EC and Regulation 2019/1010. Prospectively (ideally from 2029), all Rhineland-Palatinate SPAs are to be recorded in a six-year reporting cycle in accordance with a standardised monitoring concept (not part of this contract). Monitoring in EU Special Protection Areas 2011 the State Working Group of Bird Protection Stations (LAG VSW), together with the Umbrella Organisation of German Avifaunists (DDA) and the Federal Agency for Nature Conservation (BfN), has presented recommendations for the monitoring of European bird species and their habitats (LAG VSW et al., 2011). These pursue the goal of formulating a nationwide uniform standard for data collection. In this context, the principles mentioned for monitoring in SPAs leave sufficient room for state-specific adjustments. The results of the monitoring form the basis for site management against the background of the respective conservation objectives and for the reporting obligation under Art. 12 of Directive 2009/147/EC. Furthermore, they serve as a reference for decisions in preliminary and compatibility assessments. signal.title: MBT Crane Condition Survey
signal.description: Dumfries & Galloway Council are seeking a suitably qualified and experienced organisation ideally with an engineering background to undertake a comprehensive crane condition / reliability survey. Dumfries and Galloway Council operate a Mechanical Biological Waste Treatment facility located in Dumfries. The plant operates with 2 overhead gantry cranes which are used to lift and transfer waste around the fully automated waste treatment facility which has been in situ since 2006. The completed survey is intended to inform the Council of the cranes current condition, any immediate remedial action necessary and set out the requirements for future annual maintenance and servicing. Lot 1: . Dumfries and Galloway Council operate a Mechanical Biological Waste Treatment facility located in Dumfries. Construction on the site started in 2004 and was completed in 2006. The plant operates with 2 overhead gantry cranes which are used to lift and transfer waste around the fully automated waste treatment facility The plant was designed and constructed by Italian company Systema Ecodeco and operates with 2 Demag waste handling cranes, overhead electric top-running crane with a single hoist trolley unit. Technical specification document can be provided, however, overview of the cranes is: Manufacturing year 2006 Date of commissioning 2006 Serial number GS1442 & GS1443 Customer’s crane identification CP1 & CP2 Rated load 6.3 t Span 20.05 m Length of the runway ?? m Lifting height 11.8 m Type of the crane - Double girder EOT with one trolley Location in the customer’s process - Waste Hall Type of control - Automated Operating method - VFD Hoist - VFD Trolley - VFD Bridge Weights Trolley weight - 4.0 t No. of trolleys -1 Bridge weight - 20.0 t Non-fixed LLA weight - 0 t Fixed LLA weight - 3.5 t Design standards, classifications and speeds Crane structures - FEM 1.001 -1987 Trolley structures - A8 Movements - A8 Hoisting - 30 m/min / 1.0 m/min – M8 Trolley - 70 m/min / 1.0 m/min – M8 Bridge - 120 m/min / 1.0 m/min – M7 We are seeking to engage with a suitably qualified engineering company to undertake a comprehensive crane reliability study for both cranes currently in operation. The scope of works should include, but not be limited to, the following: - Internal endoscopic inspection and vibration analysis of the hoist gearboxes. - Vibration analysis of the rope drum, trolley wheels, hoist motor, trolley motor/gearbox, bridge motors/gearboxes and bridge wheels to determine the level of internal component degradation. - Measurement of the bridge and trolley wheels and compare to OEM specification. - Insulation and winding resistance measurements on all motors. - Rope drum inspection using specialist tools to measure the amount of wear present in the contact surfaces. - Disassembly, thorough cleaning and measurement of the internal components of the hoist, trolley and bridge brake units and compare to OEM specification. - General crane control panel electrical component condition analysis to include thorough examination of the trolley festoon mechanics, power and control flatform cables and hoist encoder cable. - Carry out thermal imaging surveys in addition to the component condition analysis to further determine problematic areas prior to potential failure. - Provide a comprehensive Crane Reliability Study structured report detailing all recommendations, corrective actions and remedial repairs. - All/Any supporting documentation. - A Geometric Survey or equivalent to provide accurate information detailing the alignment and the square of a crane. The scope of the survey should include wheels, guide rollers, end trucks, girders, and other components of the crane. - A 3D Runway Survey or equivalent to deliver accurate information on the alignment of the crane runway and expert recommendations for any needed corrective actions.. The Council requests that only organisations with the relevant capability, experience and qualifications register interest in this notice. Any feedback that can be offered is welcomed.

There are 2 lanes from the Puddefjord Bridge, whilst there are 1 lanes from O.J. Brochs gate. These meet in the tunnel so that there are 3 lanes at the exit and entrance at Nygårdstangen. The annual daily traffic is approx. 45,000. The tunnel shall be upgraded in accordance with the tunnel safety regulations and equipment in and outside the tunnel shall be replaced and replaced with new equipment that meets the current requirements. This includes, among other things: • New ventilation system. • New lighting installations with both new lights in the tunnel roof and continuous evacuation lights. • Extinguishing water shall be set up for the fire brigade. New system for handling emissions and tunnel washing water that fulfils emission requirements. • New signage with barriers, lane signal and variable signs. • Emergency stations with fire extinguishers and telephones. • Camera with coverage throughout the entire tunnel, which gives an alarm during events. • New technical building in the tunnel in the existing mountain room. • A new stop section shall be established at the technical building. • Demolition of existing air treatment plant.

signal.title: Gebäudeautomation
signal.description: Der Landkreis Nienburg/Weser plant den Neubau einer Feuerwehrtechnischen Zentrale (FTZ) im Gewerbegebiet des Ortes Lemke, Gemeinde Marklohe. Es handelt sich um einen Ersatzneubau für die bestehende FTZ in der Verdener Landstraße in Nienburg. Das Raumprogramm umfasst ca. 8.200 m2 Nutzflächen, sowie ca. 9.140 m2 Außenbereiche – Bewegungs- und Übungsflächen. Hierzu steht ein ca. 3,4 ha großes Baufeld zur Verfügung. Im Rahmen des Projektes ist die Errichtung einer Gebäudeautomationsanlage vorgesehen. Die Gebäudeautomation umfasst die Automations-, Raumautomations- und Managementebene zur Überwachung, Steuerung, Regelung und Visualisierung der technischen Anlagen. Im Projekt sind zwei zentrale Automationsschwerpunkte vorgesehen. Ergänzend hierzu werden jeweils Automationsschwerpunkte in der Fahrzeughalle, Werkstatthalle und Logistikhalle verortet. Für die Raumautomation werden in den jeweiligen Unterverteilungsbereichen der Elektrotechnik Raumautomationsverteiler angeordnet. Diese Raumautomationsverteiler bilden die Funktionen der Raumautomation ab. Die Einbindung der Sonnenschutzantriebe, Fensterkontakte sowie der Ventile der Fußbodenheizung erfolgt über I/O-Module, welche auf die Raumautomationsverteiler aufgeschaltet werden. Die Beleuchtung wird über KNX-DALI-Aktoren eingebunden, welche in den Unterverteilungen der Elektrotechnik installiert werden. Die jeweiligen Schnittstellen und Kommunikationswege sind mit den Gewerken Elektrotechnik und Gebäudeautomation entsprechend abzustimmen. Für die Anlagentechnik sind im Projekt ca. 500 physikalische Datenpunkte sowie ca. 550 gemeinsame Datenpunkte vorgesehen. Im Bereich der Raumautomation sind ca. 700 physikalische Datenpunkte sowie ca. 2.000 gemeinsame Datenpunkte vorhanden.

translation.description: Der Landkreis Nienburg/Weser plans the new construction of a fire brigade technical centre (FTZ) in the commercial area of the town of Lemke, municipality of Marklohe. This is a replacement building for the existing FTZ in Verdener Landstraße in Nienburg. The room programme comprises approx. 8.200 m2 of usable space, as well as approx. 9.140 m2 of outdoor areas – movement and exercise areas. A building site with an area of approx. 3,4 ha is available for this purpose. As part of the project, the erection of a building automation system is planned. Building automation comprises the automation, room automation and management level for monitoring, control, regulation and visualisation of the technical systems. Two central automation focuses are planned in the project. In addition to this, automation focuses are located in the vehicle hall, workshop hall and logistics hall respectively. For room automation, room automation distributors are arranged in the respective sub-distribution areas of electrical engineering. These room automation distributors map the functions of room automation. The integration of sun protection actuators, window contacts and the valves of the underfloor heating is carried out via I/O modules, which are connected to the room automation distributors. Lighting is integrated via KNX-DALI actuators installed in the electrical engineering sub-distributions. The respective interfaces and communication paths are to be coordinated accordingly with the electrical engineering and building automation trades. For the system technology, approx. 500 physical data points and approx. 550 shared data points are planned in the project. In the area of room automation, approx. 700 physical data points and approx. 2.000 shared data points are present.
translation.title: Building automation

signal.title: Claude D. Pepper Older Americans Independence Centers
signal.description: The National Institute on Aging intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to solicit applications for the Claude D. Pepper Older Americans Independence Centers (OAICs) award. The goal of the OAIC program is to establish centers of excellence in geriatrics research and research education to increase scientific knowledge leading to better ways to maintain or restore independence in older persons. OAIC awards are designed to develop or strengthen programs that focus on, and sustain progress in, a key area of aging research related to the mission of the OAIC program. Applicants should identify an area of focus in which progress could contribute to greater independence for substantial populations of older persons and offer opportunities for education in aging research. This area of focus should be a common theme around which all proposed OAIC activities are organized. Applications are not being solicited at this time. Notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects. This NOFO will utilize the P30 activity code. Investigators with expertise and insights into this area of aging research are encouraged to begin to consider applying for this new NOFO.

signal.title: Event Management System
signal.description: Background Innovate UK Business Connect brings together businesses, researchers, investors and partners to accelerate innovation across the UK. As part of UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), and a strategic delivery partner to Innovate UK, we connect organisations to funding opportunities, partnerships and expertise to help ideas move from concept to scale. One of the key tools for making these connections is events. We deliver a diverse portfolio of in-person, virtual and hybrid events, ranging from webinars and workshops to large-scale conferences and exhibitions. To support the effective planning, delivery and evaluation of these events, we are seeking proposals from suppliers who can provide a modern event management system that streamlines event operations, enhances the participant experience and supports data-driven decision-making. Description of work Innovate UK Business Connect is seeking tenders from providers who can supply a single event management system that supports the end-to-end event lifecycle, including event creation, registration management, attendee communications, speaker and exhibitor management, networking, reporting and post-event evaluation. The system should integrate with existing business systems where required and provide a single source of truth for event delivery teams. This aligns with the organisation's wider objective of ensuring events are outcome-led, measurable and supported by efficient registration, communication and reporting processes. The event management system should: • Deliver an intuitive and user-friendly delegate journey from registration through to post-event follow-up • Improve the event experience for speakers and exhibitors • Reduce manual administration and improve operational efficiency • Provide real-time visibility of registrations, attendance, engagement and event performance • Support both virtual and in-person event delivery models • Enable consistent data capture and reporting to demonstrate event impact and ROI • Support accessibility, compliance and data protection requirements The platform must support multiple user roles and permission levels to reflect different operational needs across the organisation. As a minimum, the system should accommodate the following user groups: • Event Managers o Full end-to-end event management capabilities o Creation, configuration and administration of events o Management of registrations, attendee communications, speakers and exhibitors o Access to event-level reporting, analytics and post-event evaluation data • Marketing Managers o Access to update and manage event webpages and associated content o Access to registration, engagement and performance reporting • Integrated Systems o Administration of integrations between the event management platform and our CRM system (Workbooks) o Management of data flows, field mapping, data quality and synchronisation processes o Access to reporting, data exports and system configuration relating to integrations • System Administrators o A small number of designated super users (typically two to three individuals) o Full platform administration rights, including user management, permissions, integrations, security settings and system configuration We deliver a large and diverse portfolio of business-to-business events. Historically, this has included more than 300 events per year and generating approximately 60,000 delegate registrations annually. The event management platform must be capable of supporting a range of event formats, scales and audience sizes, including: • In person events: We deliver approximately 100 in-person events each year, typically attracting between 30 and 2,000 delegates to each. Most events are free to attend and may span one or more days. We do not require onsite event delivery support from the appointment supplier; however the platform must provide the functionality and tools to enable our team to manage attendee registration and onsite event operations, and provide a seamless and efficient onsite experience for attendees • Online Events: We deliver close to 200 fully online events annually. The majority are webinars, including webinar series and interactive workshops. We also run a small number of larger-scale virtual conferences and exhibitions, some of which take place over multiple days. The platform should provide a seamless user experience for both organisers and attendees and support the delivery of events of varying size and complexity. • Hybrid: A smaller proportion of our events are hybrid, combining in-person and virtual attendance. The platform should support hybrid event delivery and provide a consistent registration, communication and reporting experience across both audience groups. The proposed solution must be capable of supporting this volume of activity while providing robust registration management, attendee communications, data integration, reporting and analytics across all event formats. Timings This is a two-stage evaluation process. We will do an initially score of each supplier bid with the top two or three scoring suppliers invited to provide a demonstration. This will be the opportunity for the selected suppliers to demonstrate the setup of an event using a given scenario. Anticipated timeline: • October: demo • November: final evaluation • November - December: Contract is awarded • 1 April 2027: Contract starts • April - September: Onboarding, training, templates created and integrations built • September onwards: Events start to be managed from the platform Cost The maximum value of this requirement over the three-year period is a maximum of £600,000.00 excluding VAT. This contract is structured as an initial two-year period with a maximum budget of £400,000.00 excluding VAT with an optional 12-month extension valued at maximum £200,000.00 excluding VAT. Submission In response to this tender, please provide the information listed below. • Short narrative describing your overall approach to working with Innovate UK Business Connect • Checklist against the requirements • Supporting information against the essential requirements • A rate card of costs associated with services you provide • A completed copy of the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire including: o A copy of your audited accounts for the most recent two years (or alternative means of demonstrating financial status if trading for less than a year) • Legal information i.e. Your standard T&Cs Please provide the information requested above to re.support@iukbc.org.uk by 17:00 10 October 2026 at the latest. IR35 will be assessed before the awarding of a successful contract. Submissions sent without relevant documents as listed above will be automatically rejected. Innovate UK Business Connect may require successful submissions to be subject to non-disclosure agreements. Evaluation structure Submissions will be scored against the following areas: • Value for money - 20% • Technical specification - 70% o alignment to objective 10% o essential requirements 40% o desirable requirements 20% • Demonstration - 10% Lot 1: .

signal.title: Deer Vehicle Collision Data Collation and Analysis Project
signal.description: NatureScot has a requirement to place a contract with an external service provider for the provision of Deer Vehicle Collision Data Collation and Analysis Project, 2025 – 2028. NatureScot, in conjunction with Transport Scotland (Scotland’s national transport agency) requires the collation, analysis and reporting of data relating to deer vehicle collisions (DVCs) in Scotland to help improve our knowledge of DVCs across the Scottish road network and to inform decision making regarding the implementation of DVC mitigation measures. Lot 1: . NatureScot, in partnership with Transport Scotland, has been running the Deer Vehicle Collision (DVC) Project since 2008. The previous phase incorporated data to the end of 2024. The purpose of the project is to collect and collate data, analyse that data and then provide information to NatureScot, Transport Scotland, Road Operating Companies, local authorities and local deer managers to assist them with decision-making around the allocation of resources and delivery of actions to reduce the number of DVCs and thereby reduce risks to public safety and safeguard deer welfare.. signal.title: The Provision of a Fraud Case Management System and Intelligence Database on behalf of NHS Counter Fraud Authority (NHSCFA)
signal.description: The NHS Counter Fraud Authority (NHSCFA) is a health authority charged with identifying, investigating and preventing fraud and other economic crime within the NHS and the wider health group. As a health authority focused entirely on counter fraud work, the NHSCFA is independent from other NHS bodies and directly accountable to the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC). THE NHSCFA currently operate two separate systems for the provision of an intelligence database and a case management system. The intention is to identify if there is a single solution that can replace the existing systems. If that is not possible then the aim would be to have two separate products that connect and align with each other to avoid duplication and operational inefficiencies. This market engagement exercise seeks the views and opinions of those organisations that may be interested in delivering the requirements. The scope of this market engagement covers is provided within the draft service specification. This exercise and any subsequent responses are in no way legally binding on any party. Participation in the engagement exercise is not a mandatory requirement for participating in any potential future procurement; however, responses received will assist to inform the Contracting Authority as to the level of interest from the market and will be used to evidence a decision as to whether or not to undertake a competitive procurement. The Market Engagement Questionnaire and current Service Specifications can be downloaded from SAP Ariba Portal at the below link: https://discovery.ariba.com/rfx/23496944 Please return your completed MEQ through the Portal no later than 5pm on 30 October 2025.

signal.title: Development and Testing of a Multi-use Frameworks Playbook for Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) (U01 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)
signal.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges. The purpose of this NOFO is to solicit applications for the design, development, and preliminary validation of robust frameworks for the application of multimodal-artificial intelligence (AI) models for clinical use. Frameworks developed through these awards would populate a "playbook", defined as a collection of actionable guidelines, standardized protocols, and/or standard operating procedures (SOPs) for reliable and effective development and deployment of multimodal AI tools. It is expected that the frameworks delineated in this playbook will directly address PRIMED-AI objectives and needs, while also remaining flexible enough to enable sufficient extensibility and interoperability for use across a broad spectrum of multimodal biomedical AI applications, both internal and external to the PRIMED-AI Program.

signal.title: COMPRA PÚBLICA DE TECNOLOGÍA INNOVADORA, DE UN SERVICIO DE ANÁLISIS, DISEÑO, DESARROLLO E IMPLANTACIÓN DE UN SISTEMA DE COORDINACIÓN DE AGENTES INTELIGENTES (CoVA) APLICADOS A LA ASISTENCIA INTERGENERACIONAL PARA LA ADMINISTRACIÓN DEL PRINCIPADO DE ASTURIAS, EN EL MARCO DEL PROYECTO EUROPA DIGITAL (DIGITAL) FINANCIADO EN UN 60% POR EL PROGRAMA OPERATIVO FEDER ASTURIAS 2021-2027
signal.description: El objeto del presente contrato son los SERVICIOS DE ANÁLISIS, DISEÑO, DESARROLLO E IMPLANTACIÓN DE UN SISTEMA DE COORDINACIÓN VIRTUAL DE AGENTES (CoVA) APLICADOS A LA ASITENCIA INTERGENERACIONAL PARA LA ADMINISTRACIÓN DEL PRINCIPADO DE ASTURIAS que permita una administración proactiva y eficiente, abarcando tanto los procesos como las personas y la tecnología necesaria para un adecuado uso, seguridad y manejo de la misma. Este contrato se enmarca en la Compra Pública de Tecnología Innovadora, (CPTI), su objeto tiene un contenido innovador y emplea especificaciones funcionales, y no requisitos técnicos: Se orienta a la adquisición de un servicio que no existe en el Principado de Asturias, pero puede desarrollarse en un tiempo razonable, dado que la tecnología está en un grado de desarrollo que así lo permite. Las tareas principales incluidas en este contrato son las siguientes: a. Implementación de un sistema de coordinación virtual de agentes basados en inteligencia artificial aplicados a la asistencia intergeneracional para la Administración del Principado de Asturias que permita el aprovechamiento de los datos generados y gestionados. b. Todos los servicios necesarios para la puesta en marcha de los elementos contratados, suscripciones/licencias necesarias, así como su gestión y mantenimiento durante la fase piloto de demostración. c. El aprovechamiento del potencial de los datos de la Administración del Principado de Asturias (en adelante, APA) para implementar nuevas formas de gestión pública basada en la interoperabilidad y analítica de datos. d. Establecer las bases tecnológicas y procedimentales para la implantación de una Administración proactiva que permita la optimización del gasto público maximizando su rendimiento. e. El desarrollo de técnicas/reglas para la gestión automatizada y clasificación de datos, documentos y expedientes mediante técnicas avanzadas de Inteligencia Artificial. f. La incorporación de técnicas de aprendizaje profundo (Deep Learning) ya que en estos procesos de digitalización pueden producir inmensas cantidades de datos para el entrenamiento y así poder dar un procesamiento que incremente la eficiencia, la eficacia y la inteligencia en el tratamiento de los datos en los procesos de las Administraciones Públicas. g. La creación de un espacio de datos corporativo que incluya los datos en origen, aquellos que se hayan podido inferir durante en el ámbito de uso del sistema, así como facilitar la interoperabilidad y circuitos de tramitación administrativa. h. Creación de un entono de atención y asistencia proactiva con la ciudadanía. i. Creación de un sandbox especializado que sirva de entorno de ideación y para la experimentación. j. Integración con el sistema de tramitación electrónica de expedientes (SITE) de la APA, y otras aplicaciones y sistemas indicados en este pliego. k. Asegurar la cadena de suministro de la inteligencia artificial (IA), para lo que se implementarán las medidas para garantizar la integridad y seguridad de los modelos de inteligencia artificial en todas las etapas, componentes y datos utilizados, con estricto cumplimiento legal del Reglamento UE 2024/1689, y cumplimiento con el decreto 98/2025 que regula el uso de la inteligencia artificial en la Administración del Principado de Asturias.

translation.description: The purpose of this contract is the SERVICES FOR THE ANALYSIS, DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A VIRTUAL AGENT COORDINATION SYSTEM (CoVA) APPLIED TO INTERGENERATIONAL ASSISTANCE FOR THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE PRINCIPALITY OF ASTURIAS which enables a proactive and efficient administration, covering both processes and people and the technology necessary for its proper use, security and management. This contract is part of Public Procurement of Innovative Technology (CPTI), its purpose has an innovative content and employs functional specifications, rather than technical requirements: It is aimed at the acquisition of a service that does not exist in the Principality of Asturias, but can be developed in a reasonable time, given that the technology is at a degree of development that allows it to do so. The main tasks included in this contract are the following: a. Implementation of a virtual agent coordination system based on artificial intelligence applied to intergenerational assistance for the Administration of the Principality of Asturias that allows the exploitation of the data generated and managed. b. All services necessary for the commissioning of the contracted elements, necessary subscriptions/licences, as well as their management and maintenance during the pilot demonstration phase. c. The exploitation of the potential of the data of the Administration of the Principality of Asturias (hereinafter, APA) to implement new forms of public management based on interoperability and data analytics. d. Establish the technological and procedural bases for the implementation of a proactive administration that allows the optimisation of public expenditure while maximising its performance. e. The development of techniques/rules for the automated management and classification of data, documents and files using advanced Artificial Intelligence techniques. f. The incorporation of deep learning techniques since these digitalisation processes can produce immense amounts of data for training and thus be able to provide processing that increases efficiency, effectiveness and intelligence in the processing of data in the processes of Public Administrations. g. The creation of a corporate data space that includes origin data, those that may have been inferred during the scope of use of the system, as well as facilitating interoperability and administrative processing circuits. h. Creation of a proactive care and assistance environment with citizens. i. Creation of a specialised sandbox that serves as an ideation and experimentation environment. j. Integration with the APA's electronic file processing system (SITE), and other applications and systems indicated in these specifications. k. Ensuring the artificial intelligence (AI) supply chain, for which measures will be implemented to guarantee the integrity and security of the artificial intelligence models at all stages, components and data used, with strict legal compliance with EU Regulation 2024/1689, and compliance with the decree 98/2025 regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the Administration of the Principality of Asturias.
