translation.description: The tender process comprises the conclusion of one (1) contract regarding the Contracting Authority's procurement of the development of an AI-based simulation tool for training child interviews. Based on this tender, one (1) joint contract will be concluded between the supplier and the Responsible Contracting Authority, cf. point 1.2 of the tender conditions, which acts on behalf of all participating contracting authorities. The Responsible Contracting Authority is Professionshøjskolen Absalon, which is authorised to manage all rights and obligations under the contract and acts as the contracting party towards the supplier. The supplier may therefore only direct claims against the Responsible Contracting Authority. Other participating contracting authorities are not direct contracting parties and are not liable either individually or jointly for the performance of the contract. Professionshøjskolen Absalon, in collaboration with the other university colleges, Red Barnet, Barndom Uden Vold and Ole Kirk’s Fond, is offering a contract for the development of an AI-based simulation tool, which is referred to in the tender documentation as the Solution. The purpose is to strengthen the competencies of social workers and social work students to conduct interviews with children in vulnerable situations, including children who may have been exposed to violence or abuse. The Solution must create a realistic, safe and learning-oriented training environment where users can prepare for child interviews, conduct interviews with digital avatars, receive guidance and feedback from a Tutor and subsequently analyse their interviews for the purpose of learning and reflection. It must be capable of being used in social work education, in continuing and further education programmes and in municipal practice. The first version, which this tender covers, must provide the possibility for speech- and text-based interaction with four avatars aged 9–11 years, representing different backgrounds and case types. In addition, there is a Tutor who supports the user before, during and after the interview through preparatory information, ongoing professional hints and subsequent debriefing. The Solution must accommodate both full interview processes and shorter modules where individual interview techniques can be trained in isolation. In the long term, the ambition is to expand the solution with more advanced modalities such as facial expressions and body language as well as real-time analysis of non-verbal communication. The Contracting Authority therefore wishes to attract suppliers who can not only deliver the tendered solution but can also think visionarily in terms of creating a future-proof and innovative platform. The Responsible Contracting Authority provides an extensive knowledge base in the form of practice-oriented cases, anonymised child interviews and the expertise of professionals, and will also contribute actively with professional sparring during development. The tenders will be evaluated on feasibility and risk assessment, functionality and security, the realism of the avatars, the professional quality of the tutor as well as the overall user experience and technical robustness. The Responsible Contracting Authority is entitled to terminate the contract at Partial Delivery Day 1 (POC), solely for the purpose of bringing the project to an end, if it turns out during Partial Delivery 1 - POC that there are technical challenges which make it impossible to develop a suitable and usable Solution for the purpose that the contract supports, cf. point 31.2.1 of the Contract. However, it is the clear intention of the Responsible Contracting Authority to complete the development of a complete Solution that functions according to its purpose. Due to the established budget, the Contracting Authority has set a price ceiling for the Delivery Consideration. The Delivery Consideration, including the price for the Clarification Phase and the Delivery, cf. Contract Annex 01 – Schedule, must thus be a maximum of five (5) million DKK excl. VAT. Within the established price ceiling of five (5) million DKK excl. VAT, the Contracting Authority wishes to promote solutions that combine high technical quality and a high level of innovation. With this tender, the Contracting Authority aims to support a competition that is not only based on price, but also on the Tenderers' ability to think long-term and visionarily. The Contracting Authority therefore explains the strategic and technological ambitions for the Solution in order to encourage tenderers to present proposals that reflect a future-proof and technologically advanced approach. At the same time, it is important for the Contracting Authority that the Solution can be operated sustainably within the financial frameworks that apply to the joint operations of the university colleges. The Contracting Authority therefore wishes to enter into a contract with a Supplier who can ensure creativity and technical ingenuity in relation to developing a Solution that meets the desired needs, but which can at the same time be operated by the university colleges jointly - where interview flow is weighted higher than visualisation of the child's non-verbal language.
translation.title: Tender with negotiation regarding the development of an AI-based simulation tool for training in child interviews

signal.description: Transparenzbekanntmachung im Sinne des § 135 Abs. 3 GWB Maßnahme: Anschaffung der Software OK. Verkehr für die Fahrzeugzulassung und Betrieb im Rechenzentrum für Fahrzeugzulassung und Fahrerlaubnis Informationen über die Überprüfungsfristen: Hinsichtlich der Fristen zur Einlegung von Rechtsbehelfen wird auf § 160 Abs. 3 des Gesetzes gegen Wettbewerbsbeschränkungen (GWB) verwiesen. § 160 GWB lautet wie folgt: (1) Die Vergabekammer leitet ein Nachprüfungsverfahren nur auf Antrag ein. (2) Antragsbefugt ist jedes Unternehmen, das ein Interesse an dem öffentlichen Auftrag oder der Konzession hat und eine Verletzung in seinen Rechten nach § 97 Abs. 6 durch Nichtbeachtung von Vergabevorschriften geltend macht. Dabei ist darzulegen, dass dem Unternehmen durch die behauptete Verletzung der Vergabevorschriften einSchaden entstanden ist oder zu entstehen droht. (3) Der Antrag ist unzulässig, soweit: 1) der Antragsteller den geltend gemachten Verstoß gegen Vergabevorschriften vor Einreichen des Nachprüfungsantrags erkannt und gegenüber dem Auftraggeber nicht innerhalb einer Frist von 10 Kalendertagen gerügt hat; der Ablauf der Frist nach § 134 Absatz 2 bleibt unberührt, 2) Verstöße gegen Vergabevorschriften, die aufgrund der Bekanntmachung erkennbar sind, nicht spätestens bis zum Ablauf der in der Bekanntmachung benannten Frist zur Bewerbung oder Angebotsabgabe gegenüber dem Auftraggeber gerügt werden, 3)Verstöße gegen Vergabevorschriften, die erst in den Vergabeunterlagen erkennbar sind, nicht spätestens bis zum Ablauf der Frist zur Bewerbung oder zur Angebotsabgabe gegenüber dem Auftraggeber gerügt werden, 4) mehr als 15 Kalendertage nach Eingang der Mitteilung des Auftraggebers, einer Rüge nicht abhelfen zu wollen, vergangen sind. Satz 1 gilt nicht bei einem Antrag auf Feststellung der Unwirksamkeit des Vertrages nach § 135 Abs. 1 Nr. 2. §134 Abs. 1 Satz 2 bleibt unberührt. Der Auftrag kann nur von einem bestimmten Wirtschaftsteilnehmer ausgeführt werden, da hier gem. §14 Abs. 4 Nr. 2b VgV aus technischen Gründen nur ein Unternehmen für den Auftrag in Betracht kommt.

translation.description: Transparency notice within the meaning of § 135 para. 3 of the Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB) Measure: Acquisition of the software OK.Verkehr for vehicle registration and operation in the data centre for vehicle registration and driving licences Information on review periods: Regarding the deadlines for filing legal remedies, reference is made to § 160 para. 3 of the Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB). § 160 GWB reads as follows: (1) The Public Procurement Chamber shall initiate a review procedure only upon application. (2) Any undertaking that has an interest in the public contract or concession and claims an infringement of its rights under § 97 para. 6 due to non-compliance with procurement regulations is entitled to file an application. In doing so, it must be demonstrated that the undertaking has suffered or is threatened with damage as a result of the alleged infringement of procurement regulations. (3) The application is inadmissible if: 1) the applicant has recognised the alleged infringement of procurement regulations before submitting the application for review and has not complained about it to the contracting authority within a period of 10 calendar days; the expiry of the period according to § 134 paragraph 2 remains unaffected, 2) infringements of procurement regulations that are recognisable from the notice are not complained about to the contracting authority by the expiry of the deadline for application or submission of tenders specified in the notice, 3) infringements of procurement regulations that only become recognisable in the procurement documents are not complained about to the contracting authority by the expiry of the deadline for application or submission of tenders, 4) more than 15 calendar days have passed since receipt of the notification from the contracting authority that it does not intend to remedy a complaint. Sentence 1 does not apply to an application for a declaration of the ineffectiveness of the contract pursuant to § 135 para. 1 no. 2. § 134 para. 1 sentence 2 remains unaffected. The contract can only be executed by a specific economic operator, as here, pursuant to § 14 para. 4 no. 2b of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV), only one company can be considered for the contract for technical reasons.

signal.title: Resourcing the AI Adoption Programme
signal.description: Greater London government (the GLA Group) is accelerating AI adoption through a common approach to governance, capability and usage​. AI tools are already in use across the GLA group. We are looking to standardise our approach, guidance and governance. ​Our goal is to create the conditions for a well-governed and responsible adoption at scale The GLA Group is exploring the market for an external partner to work with us to shape our AI Adoption Programme cohesively ahead of delivery, in areas where external expertise would add great value to align our policies and co-design training, to responsibly support AI pilots and scale successful pilots across departments and organisations. ​ The requirement is expected to include: Develop and embed London AI principles in organisational policy:​ Develop London-specific AI principles common for the entire GLA Group based on the UK Government's AI Playbook. Embed these principles in each organisation's policies, (incl. those which are not AI-specific and in procurement standards) and operationalise these principles in our culture and practice to ensure responsible and innovative AI use.​ Envision and validate a 'to-be' position on AI best practice ensuring we lead by example on the recommendations in the London AI and Jobs Taskforce report (incl. using our role as an employer and procurer to shape AI adoption and workforce transition in London). Design and deliver a practical tiered training offer:​ For all staff, on what AI can do well, risks and responsibilities, everyday productivity uses and improving prompting.​ For specific teams targeted for having tasks apt for simplification from AI, tailored training on role-specific use cases, practical exercises, measuring benefits and feeding back potential projects and pilots.​ For leadership, organisational changes, strategic opportunities, governance and risk management. Support us in co-designing an operating model for the future of AI Adoption​: Co-design an evaluation framework to confirm which opportunities to pilot and which successful use cases to scale within and across organisations Lot 1: .
